analysis.investment_thesis: Datamatics is a financially conservative mid-tier IT-BPM player with a clean balance sheet and an interesting AI/RPA product portfolio, but 8.7% revenue CAGR and 12.5% ROE fall well short of my compounding standards for a high-conviction India tech bet. At 20x P/E it is fairly priced, not cheaply priced, making a fresh entry unattractive relative to faster-growing IT alternatives.
key_strengths: Clean balance sheet with D/E of only 0.13 and net cash positive (INR 218 Cr cash vs INR 190 Cr total debt)
Net profit CAGR of 18.4% over 9 years driven by steady margin expansion — from INR 45 Cr (FY16) to INR 206 Cr (FY25)
Strong promoter conviction at 66.33% holding with consistent OCF — 5/5 years positive, INR 201 Cr FCF in FY25
key_risks: Revenue growth too slow at 8.7% CAGR — well below my 15%+ threshold for tech compounders; top-line momentum is decelerating
ROE of 12.5% and ROCE of 15% are sub-par for an IT company — capital is not being sweated hard enough
Operating income and EBITDA actually declined YoY in FY25 (INR 244→232 Cr and INR 271→256 Cr) — margin compression at the worst time
red_flags: Other income of INR 78 Cr in FY25 represents ~38% of net profit — earnings quality is diluted by non-operating items
Borrowings surged from INR 17 Cr (FY24) to INR 186 Cr (FY25) with no clear large acquisition disclosed — needs explanation
Institutional interest almost zero (FII 0.48%, DII 0.11%) — the market has seen this story and is not excited
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Datamatics has been a steady business since 1975 — reliable but not a compounding machine. Revenue grew from INR 816 Cr (FY16) to INR 1,723 Cr (FY25) at a mere 8.7% CAGR, which in today's AI-driven IT market is pedestrian. The AI/RPA product suite (TruBot, TruCap+, TruBI) is interesting branding, but the revenue numbers show these are not yet breakout growth drivers. Operating margins of 14.55% are acceptable for BPM-heavy IT but leave no room for error, and FY25 saw both operating income and EBITDA decline year-on-year — not the direction I want to see when I'm paying 20x earnings.

What concerns me most as Jhunjhunwala is the earnings quality. INR 78 Cr of other income in FY25 — up from INR 45 Cr in FY24 — is carrying a meaningful portion of net profit. The sudden jump in borrowings to INR 186 Cr from just INR 17 Cr the prior year, with investing cash outflows matching operating cash inflows rupee for rupee, suggests an acquisition or investment cycle that needs scrutiny. ROE of 12.5% means the business is retaining capital but not generating adequate returns on it. For the India IT growth story, I would rather own companies with 20%+ ROE and 18%+ revenue growth — Datamatics is a B-grade business at a B-grade price, not a steal.
